name: GHRP-6
route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
status: Not FDA-approved; FDA Category 3 (nominated without adequate support) and safety concerns cited; banned in sport
mechanism: A six-amino-acid peptide, the first of its family studied widely in people, that activates the ghrelin receptor to release growth hormone

article.summary: GHRP-6 is a six-amino-acid peptide that triggers growth hormone release and hunger. Human data are short hormone studies; it is unapproved, the FDA cites safety concerns, and WADA bans it.
article.takeaway: GHRP-6 is a synthetic six-amino-acid peptide that triggers growth hormone release by acting on a receptor later found to be the target of ghrelin, the stomach hunger hormone.[^1][^2] In 18 healthy men it released growth hormone strongly and worked synergistically with GHRH, but at the highest dose it also doubled prolactin and cortisol.[^1] It has no FDA approval; the FDA has cited possible effects on cortisol and blood sugar, and WADA bans it.[^3][^4]
glance: Not approved; FDA Category 3 for compounding, with safety concerns cited[^3][^5]
Injection in research and gray-market use; no approved dosing
Prohibited at all times; WADA names GHRP-6[^4]

blocks.text: GHRP-6 was the first synthetic GH-releasing peptide studied extensively in people. It acts on a receptor unrelated to the GHRH receptor, and the body's own partner for that receptor, ghrelin, was identified in the stomach in 1999.[^6][^2] Combined with GHRH, GHRP-6 released more GH than either alone, which suggests the two signals work independently.[^1]

The human data are short hormone-response studies. In 18 healthy men, single intravenous doses released GH in a dose-dependent way, and low doses combined with GHRH acted synergistically. Prolactin and cortisol rose about twofold only at the highest dose, and no adverse clinical effects were observed with GHRP-6 in that study.[^1]

The searches for this entry found no trial showing that GHRP-6 builds muscle, burns fat, heals tissue or slows aging. Its close relative GHRP-2 increased food intake in healthy men, and appetite stimulation is a known effect of ghrelin-receptor agonists.[^7]

items: **FDA concerns:** immune-reaction risk from aggregation and impurities; limited data show a possible effect on cortisol and higher blood glucose from reduced insulin sensitivity[^3]
**Hormone effects:** prolactin and cortisol roughly doubled at the highest dose in men,[^1] and GHRP-6 raised ACTH and cortisol in pigs[^8]
**Appetite:** can increase hunger and food intake
**Unknown long term:** no long-term safety, cancer or mortality data exist for healthy users
**Quality:** illegally sold peptide drugs have shown highly variable amounts, low purity and toxic metals such as arsenic and lead[^9]

blocks.text: GHRP-6 is not FDA-approved. The FDA's May 2026 list places it in Category 3, nominated without adequate support, which is not an endorsement for compounding.[^5] The FDA's safety page also describes concerns about GHRP-6 for outsourcing facilities, first listed in September 2023.[^3] WADA lists GHRP-6 as a prohibited GH-releasing peptide at all times.[^4]

GHRP-6 is a historically important research peptide that reliably triggers GH release in short studies. That does not show benefits for muscle, fat loss or healing, and the FDA has flagged safety concerns. Athletes subject to testing should treat it as banned.

evidence.label: Low: short hormone studies only
evidence.text: Human work is short and measures hormone responses.[^1][^6] No outcome trials of the wellness claims were found.

faq.q: What is the difference between GHRP-6 and ghrelin?
faq.a: Ghrelin is the natural hormone made in the stomach.[^2] GHRP-6 is a synthetic peptide that acts on the same system, which explains the appetite effects seen in this drug family.

faq.q: Is GHRP-6 the same as ipamorelin?
faq.a: No. Both release GH through the ghrelin receptor, but in pigs GHRP-6 raised ACTH and cortisol while ipamorelin did not.[^8] See [ipamorelin](/peptides/ipamorelin).
Yes. WADA lists GHRP-6 as prohibited at all times.[^4]
